articles.title: This TSA-Compliant Daran 89.6Wh 100W LiFePO4 Power Station Drops to Just $49.99
articles.summary: Ahead of Black Friday, Amazon is offering the diminutive Daran 89.6Wh 100W Power Station for just $49.99 after applying coupon code " DDDD4999 ". Unlike previous iterations of this deal, you don't to be an Amazon Prime member to be eligible.
body: The Daran power station just 6.5" x 3.3" x 4" and weighs in at a portable 2.5 pounds. The 89.6W battery capacity (approximately 28,000mAh at 3.2V) is also TSA compliant, so you can bring it with you on your airplane flights.

It has a total of seven charging ports, including two 120V AC outlets (100W max), two USB-C ports (45W/15W), two USB-A ports (18W/15W), and a DC5521 port (60W). The 100W max output on the AC outlet is good for charging higher powered mobile electronics like your laptop, iPad, or handheld gaming PC, but it's also handy for older, legacy electronics that are powered by a traditional plug and not a USB cable.

The power station uses LiFePO4 cells instead of NCM cells you'd find in some other budget power stations. LiFePO4 cells have inherently safer chemistry, longer lifespan, and slower calendar aging than NCM cells. They are widely regarded as the best battery option for power stations.

Eric Song is the IGN commerce manager in charge of finding the best gaming and tech deals every day. When Eric isn't hunting for deals for other people at work, he's hunting for deals for himself during his free time.

articles.title: Amazon's Lord of the Rings Gandalf Costume Has Dropped to Its Lowest Price of the Year
articles.summary: October 31 is nearly here and time is running out to buy yourself a costume. This is the week that Spirit Halloween starts to look fully picked over and popular costumes become incredibly scarce.
body: At $36.33 for the XL size, it's surprisingly affordable for an officially licensed costume. It doesn't come with a fake beard or a wig, but if you already have either of those things then you're set. And if you don't, you should be able to find that still in stock somewhere before Halloween.

The costume you are buying here is specifically the robe, hat, and belt that were designed after the iconic wizard from Middle-earth. This is a version of Gandalf the Gray, as seen in The Hobbit movie, rather than the more majestic Gandalf the White we got in the later LOTR movies. Like most affordable costumes, it's made of 100% polyester, which means you probably don't want to toss it into the wash with the rest of your clothes.

The main issue with this costume, like I mentioned above, is that it isn't exactly complete. If you want to look like Gandalf and not just some random wizard, you will need a gray beard and a gray wig. You'll also likely want some sort of gnarled staff, which can honestly just be a cool tree branch you find in the forest. Thankfully Amazon also has a perfect wig and beard combo in stock that will arrive before Halloween.

articles.title: Here’s Another Mass Effect 5 Leak To Break Your Heart
articles.summary: If last week's mysterious Mass Effect: Universe trailer leak wasn't painful enough for you in the wake of BioWare's sudden closure, we've gotten yet another taste of The Game That Could Have Been, this time courtesy of award-winning video game composer Austin Wintory.
body: Known for his beautiful and haunting soundtracks for games like Flow, Journey, ABZÛ, Aliens: Fireteam Elite, Sword of The Sea, John Wick Hex, and Hades II, Wintory was also evidently working on the Mass Effect: Universe soundtrack. From the sounds of things, EA and the now-defunct BioWare were considering having Wintory produce the game's OST. And thanks to Wintory, we at least know what the game might have sounded like.

"Mass Effect was my ultimate white whale, my all-time dream project," Wintory wrote in a post on Bluesky. "For the last couple years I'd been in discussion with BioWare & EA to take on the project, and as part of that, I wrote close to 20 minutes of music to explore where the franchise can go next. May as well share it!"
Wintory shared the music alongside an image that reads, "Mass Effect: Universe, the music that might have been."

"So here you go," Wintory added in a follow-up post linking to a YouTube upload of the test-run tracks. "Thank you again to my friends at both BioWare and EA. To even dream in your sandbox was a privilege."
points: If last week's mysterious Mass Effect: Universe trailer leak wasn't painful enough for you in the wake of BioWare's sudden closure, we've gotten yet another taste of The Game That Could Have Been…

articles.title: WoW: Forever Just Got Another Major Racial Ability Shakeup Before Launch
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever's release is just around the corner, but developer Blizzard is making one final pass at the game's racial abilities before launch in response to beta feedback.
body: In a forum post, WoW community manager Kaivax posted a list of significant changes to many of each race's unique abilities that players expressed concerns about during Forever's beta. Those changes include tweaks to tauren, humans, orcs, dwarves, and Skyborne elves.

"In taking a final pass on these, we've prioritized racial identity, which means that some races will naturally be slightly more effective than others at certain combat roles," Blizzard said. "In some places where we had replaced role or class-focused racials with generic ones, we're rolling those changes back."

The exception to that mindset is weapon-specialization abilities, Blizzard said, which existed for humans and orcs both in WoW Classic and early on in Forever's beta and made each race more effective with specific types of weapons.

"While those have a strong fantasy component to them, it is not healthy in the long run for future raid and dungeon loot tables to be evaluated through the lens of 'required' weapon types," Blizzard said. "At the same time, we're doing a tuning pass on some of the remaining passive bonuses to help ensure that they aren't skewing outcomes in a way that limits player preferences."
points: World of Warcraft: Forever's release is just around the corner, but developer Blizzard is making one final pass at the game's racial abilities before launch in response to beta feedback.

articles.title: 24 Years Later, Nintendo's Most Divisive Mario Game Is a Miracle on Switch 2
articles.summary: I can’t remember what I had for lunch yesterday, but I still remember the day Super Mario Sunshine launched in 2002. It was a summer's day and I couldn’t wait to line up at the GameStop in the Natick Mall to pick up my pre-ordered copy.
body: In 2026, that sounds like a bit of revisionist history. These days, Sunshine is regarded as one of Nintendo’s most divisive games; it’s both overrated and underrated at the same time. Some players continue to go to war for it, praising its wealth of creative ideas. Others are proud haters who point to poor camera controls and a handful of dud levels to give its apologists a reality check. Switch 2 owners should decide for themselves, as Super Mario Sunshine is available now as part of Nintendo Switch Online’s GameCube collection.

Allow me to play the role of prosecution as you dive into Mario’s most polarizing adventure: Despite some undeniable flaws, Super Mario Sunshine is the one Mario game that best captures the ethos of the entire series. Even today, I am still happy to go to bat for one of Nintendo’s most inventive and focused games.

articles.title: Diablo 4’s War Plans Are Getting A Huge Upgrade In Season 16
articles.summary: Diablo 4's War Plans system is getting a major upgrade in Season 16, giving players even more control over their endgame activities and rewards. Developer Blizzard introduced War Plans earlier this year as part of the game's second (and last) expansion, Lord of Hatred.
body: It was a welcome addition, but unfortunately only gave players minimal control over what activities would appear as part of their plans. Players could also only reroll their War Plans a limited number of times, meaning if you didn't like a particular activity, oftentimes you were stuck having to do it.

All of that looks to be changing in Season 16 with the addition of a new meta-progression system called War Plans Tactics. By completing War Plan activities, players will be able to invest points into the tactics tree to make it so certain activities are more likely to appear and specific types of rewards will drop. How players reroll their War Plans is also changing, with a new currency called Marks of Wisdom that will cap at 20 and should let players reroll their plans more often.

"Earn points from completing War Plans activities, then invest these points into nodes to increase the chance of preferred activities or rewards appearing," Blizzard said. "This allows you to tailor your War Plans more closely with both your goals and playstyle."
points: Diablo 4's War Plans system is getting a major upgrade in Season 16, giving players even more control over their endgame activities and rewards.

articles.title: 10 Years Later, Nintendo's Switch Reveal Is a Fascinating Time Capsule
articles.summary: It seems outlandish to think about now that it’s sold 156 million units, but there was a lot of skepticism about the Nintendo Switch in October 2016.
body: The Wii U had been a massive flop, selling just 13.5 million units in its lifecycle, making it the second-worst-selling Nintendo console since the Virtual Boy. Thanks to a July 2016 Eurogamer report, observers already knew the project codenamed “Nintendo NX” was a portable system that used a docking station to connect to a TV set. To skeptics, the NX sounded underpowered compared to the PlayStation 4 and Xbox 360 — and had too much in common with the unpopular Wii U. What’s more, handheld consoles had fallen pretty dramatically out of fashion amid the rise of smartphones and free-to-play mobile games throughout the 2010s.

While some aspects of that first look haven’t aged particularly well, much of the company’s vision for the Switch remains consistent even today. A decade later, let’s take a look back at some highlights from the reveal.

articles.title: Marvel's Forgotten Mass Effect Clone Couldn't Escape the Avengers' Failure
articles.summary: The Avengers are massively successful on the big screen, with four films collectively making nearly $8 billion at the worldwide box office. But that cinematic success hasn't carried over to the video game world.
body: Avengers was the first game to come out of a collaboration between Marvel and Final Fantasy maker Square Enix. A black cloud hung over it that ended up overshadowing the next Marvel game from Square Enix: Marvel’s Guardians of the Galaxy, which was released five years ago on Oct. 26, 2021. It was better than anyone expected, yet was still a disappointment in Square Enix’s eyes.

Guardians of the Galaxy offered a new spin on the ragtag bunch made famous by the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Everyone you’re familiar with is here — Peter Quill/Star-Lord, Gamora, Rocket, Groot, and Drax — plus some comic characters who hadn’t been adapted before, like Lady Hellbender. It deftly balances universe-at-stake storytelling with more personal looks at its characters, like Quill.

While Chris Pratt’s Star-Lord may never be mature enough to have kids, Guardians of the Galaxy ’s Quill wonders throughout the game if he’s actually the father of his old Nova Corps flame’s teenage daughter, Nikki. The tension of “Is this mercenary who’s barely scraping by actually a dad?” hangs over the game, and results in some tender moments between Quill and his former lover, the Centurion Ko-Rel.
points: The Avengers are massively successful on the big screen, with four films collectively making nearly $8 billion at the worldwide box office.
But that cinematic success hasn't carried over to the video game world.

articles.title: Why There Won’t Be A Helldivers 3 Anytime Soon, If Ever
articles.summary: Helldivers 2 has been a huge hit for developer Arrowhead and publisher Sony, but don't expect a third game in the series anytime soon. Arrowhead's chief creative officer, Johan Pilestedt, told Rock Paper Shotgun that a sequel would reset "everything" and force the player to "start over." He doesn't…
body: "Some studios can treat players like a short-term cash grab," Pilestedt said. "We see players as the actual engine of the game: they're the ones bringing in friends, making memes, and keeping the game alive. When you have an active community doing that, you don’t need a sequel."

He went on to say that the video game industry today is "panicking" because "the old live-service tricks don't work anymore," and that would also apply to a hypothetical Helldivers 3. If Arrowhead were to make a sequel, it would need to be highly differentiated, he said.

"The biggest competitor to a Helldivers 3 would be Helldivers 2. It only makes sense to make a distinct sequel if it’s so different that both games can exist side by side. For now, making Helldivers 2 better every day makes way more sense than throwing away its momentum," he said.
Pilestedt added that 95% of the studio is working on Helldivers 2 right now, with only a small team assigned to work on whatever the team is making next.
points: Helldivers 2 has been a huge hit for developer Arrowhead and publisher Sony, but don't expect a third game in the series anytime soon.

articles.title: Mass Effect fans ramp up efforts to save BioWare's RPG series with a Times Square billboard and plans for more ads outside The Game Awards
articles.summary: Fans continue to rally around the 'Save Mass Effect ' movement, this time with a billboard at Times Square and more initiatives planned throughout the rest of the year.
body: Last week, publisher EA shut down BioWare and cancelled the next Mass Effect game. In the days since, an increasingly loud community-organised campaign has attempted to make Electronic Arts reverse course and ensure that the beloved sci-fi universe can journey forward in some form.

The We Are Mass Effect community group and content creator Kala Elizabeth are now collaborating on a number of initiatives, including a billboard at New York City's Times Square that points people toward the growing online "SaveMassEffect" hashtag. Text that reads "Kellah Si'yah" is sprawled across the ad - referencing the in-game ship that ferried different races to settle the Andromeda system.

"Apart from the Times Square billboard, we also have several other initiatives in the works. An advertising truck near EA's headquarters in Redwood City and in Edmonton, a mobile billboard for N7 Day, and another one in LA for The Game Awards. All of them will carry a message in support of #SaveMassEffect," one of the group's organisers, Mer Mora, told me via email.
points: Fans continue to rally around the 'Save Mass Effect ' movement, this time with a billboard at Times Square and more initiatives planned throughout the rest of the year.

articles.title: Amid sweeping layoffs at Xbox and massive AI investments, Microsoft introduces a "Voluntary Exit Offer" to 60,000 workers
articles.summary: Xbox isn't the only Microsoft division looking to massively reduce worker headcounts. In fact, Microsoft has just announced a "Voluntary Exit Offer" that will essentially pay staff to move in front of any potential layoffs and voluntarily leave their jobs.
body: Microsoft CPO Amy Coleman announced the plan earlier today. "This offer gives eligible employees who may be considering a future outside the company a new choice to make that transition now with support. It also gives participating organizations another way to adapt their workforce to changing needs," Colemon wrote in a memo sent to staff.

The voluntary buyout is only available to Microsoft employees "at level 70 and below" in Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States. Some corners of the company have opted out of the offer - it's currently unclear if Xbox or any of the studios under its umbrella are participating in the initiative.

"This is a time-limited, voluntary program that gives those who are eligible the opportunity to leave Microsoft with financial support and career planning resources. Some organizations are providing the Voluntary Exit Offer, and some are not. Participation varies based on each business’s priorities, customer commitments and workforce needs," Coleman added.
points: Xbox isn't the only Microsoft division looking to massively reduce worker headcounts.

- Gather Battery Cells and complete challenges to earn defense, damage or tactical upgrades from a collection of 12 different perks
- Choose your path through Castle Doom’s winding routes and thoughtfully select buffs to alter your combat abilities to become an unstoppable powerhouse

videos.title: DF Direct Weekly #287: Xbox Helix $1200-$1800? BioWare Shut, FSR 4 RDNA 2 + Xbox, Sony Frame Gen!
videos.summary: Many thanks to Alienware for sponsoring this video. To learn more about Alienware’s 39-inch 5K OLED Gaming Monitor, check it out here:
body: Big news this week from Fortune, with an insider feature on Xbox that combines deep access to senior management along with a range of big reveals: a Helix console costing between $1200 to $1800 coming 2028? A handheld in 2027? Disagreements between the Xbox and Microsoft OS teams? There's a lot to discuss here. Meanwhile, the team lament the end of BioWare and mull over the leaked Mass Effect trailer, and there's good news for RDNA 2 GPU owners - and Xbox Series console users - as FSR 4 arrives ahead of time. A potential PlayStation frame generation technique is discussed and finally, five years of Oliver Mackenzie at Digital Foundry! The panel look back at his first video and discuss his approach to working on the channel.

videos.title: Cult of the Lamb – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition – Launch
videos.summary: Play Cult of the Lamb – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition now:
body: Start your own cult in a land of false prophets! Venture out into diverse and mysterious regions to build a loyal community of woodland Followers, and spread your Word to become the one true cult.

The Nintendo Switch 2 version of Cult of the Lamb includes enhanced resolution, improved frame rates, and GameShare support. The upgrade will be available for free to owners of the original Switch version of Cult of the Lamb.
